checks: Interpolation of two included Euclidean balls gives the whole ball of the averaged radius at the interpolated center. The convex radius at that base is at most this radius. A finite convex function on the full real base space is continuous, so the pointwise ball-inclusion condition is closed.

Taking the maximum of each fiber linear form on its translated ball adds exactly the Euclidean norm of its continuous coefficient times r(z), with no change for a pure-base inequality. The exponential choice is convex and finite, and the inequalities at fixed base remain polyhedral.

The positive-fiber hull is inside the actual erosion, so every positive fiber is unchanged and the others remain null in d-volume. This is equality of mixed measures, including when no positive fiber survives, with the usual empty hull convention.
Matched the original source 1357de39d4196ea9 §1, (1)–(2), including the distinction between polytopal integer fibers and the real-base eroded set.

overlap.comparison: Its support-cut formula is a nearby small-parameter erosion with admissible affine base ceilings, but this statement applies to arbitrary compact convex sets, convex radii of arbitrary size and the exact ambient inequality and positive-fiber hull formulas.

readability: The statement uses the standard closed Euclidean unit ball convention. No substantive ambiguity.

summary: Variable-radius inner erosion is convex and preserves the summed mixed measure after taking the hull of its positive integer fibers.
